title: Lenny Rachitsky on How Today's Top Startups Found Product-Market Fit and Cold Starts
transcript:
Lenny: In this episode, I synthesize insights from researching over 100 top tech companies on how they actually found product-market fit (PMF) in their 0-to-1 days.

Finding product-market fit is not a binary light switch; it is a progressive journey with distinct signs. When you don't have PMF, the market is pushing you away. You're pushing water uphill. Customer acquisition is expensive, churn is brutal, and you have to constantly explain why your product is useful.

When you hit true PMF, the market starts pulling product out of you. Customers get genuinely angry when your site goes down. You see organic word of mouth where users recommend your tool without incentives.

Here are the three most reliable signals of true product-market fit across consumer and B2B products:
1. A flat retention curve: After day 30 or day 90, cohort retention stabilizes and levels out asymptotically, rather than declining down to zero.
2. Sustainable organic growth: At least 30% to 50% of new signups arrive via unprompted word-of-mouth or organic search.
3. High willingness to pay or advocate: When asked Sean Ellis's canonical test 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?', at least 40% of active users answer 'very disappointed'.

For early-stage founders facing the cold start problem, doing things that don't scale—like hand-onboarding your first 50 users, embedding yourself in niche communities, and listening obsessionally to customer friction—remains the universal secret of early traction.
